audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for hypocrisy warning, fear/courage sayings, Spirit speech, rich fool, ravens/lilies, treasure, watchfulness, faithful steward, fire/division, and discerning the time.

verses.restored: Meanwhile, when many thousands of the crowd gathered so that they trampled one another, he began to say first to his disciples, Watch yourselves from the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

familiar.text: In the mean time, when there were gathered together an innumerable multitude of people, insomuch that they trode one upon another, he began to say unto his disciples first of all, Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

modern.text: In the meantime, a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling one another. Jesus began to speak first to His disciples: “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

original.text: Ἐν οἷς ἐπισυναχθεισῶν τῶν μυριάδων τοῦ ὄχλου, ὥστε καταπατεῖν ἀλλήλους, ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ πρῶτον· Προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης, ⸂ἥτις ἐστὶν ὑπόκρισις, τῶν Φαρισαίων⸃.

verses.restored: Nothing is covered that will not be revealed, nor hidden that will not be known.

familiar.text: For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.

modern.text: There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.

original.text: οὐδὲν δὲ συγκεκαλυμμένον ἐστὶν ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται, καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται.

verses.restored: Therefore whatever you said in darkness will be heard in the light, and what you spoke into the ear in inner rooms will be proclaimed on the rooftops.

familiar.text: Therefore whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be heard in the light; and that which ye have spoken in the ear in closets shall be proclaimed upon the housetops.

modern.text: What you have spoken in the dark will be heard in the daylight, and what you have whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the housetops. Fear God Alone (Matthew 10:26–31)

original.text: ἀνθʼ ὧν ὅσα ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτὶ ἀκουσθήσεται, καὶ ὃ πρὸς τὸ οὖς ἐλαλήσατε ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις κηρυχθήσεται ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων.

verses.restored: I say to you, my friends: do not fear those who kill the body and after these things have nothing more to do.

familiar.text: And I say unto you my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.

modern.text: I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.

original.text: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν τοῖς φίλοις μου, μὴ φοβηθῆτε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεινόντων τὸ σῶμα καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα μὴ ἐχόντων περισσότερόν τι ποιῆσαι.

verses.restored: I will show you whom to fear: fear the one who, after killing, has authority to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I say to you, fear this one.

familiar.text: But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.

modern.text: But I will show you whom you should fear: Fear the One who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear Him!

original.text: ὑποδείξω δὲ ὑμῖν τίνα φοβηθῆτε· φοβήθητε τὸν μετὰ τὸ ἀποκτεῖναι ⸂ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν⸃ ἐμβαλεῖν εἰς τὴν γέενναν· ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, τοῦτον φοβήθητε.

verses.restored: Are not five sparrows sold for two small coins? Yet not one of them is forgotten before the Divine.

familiar.text: Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God?

modern.text: Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.

original.text: οὐχὶ πέντε στρουθία ⸀πωλοῦνται ἀσσαρίων δύο; καὶ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔστιν ἐπιλελησμένον ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Even the hairs of your head have all been numbered. Do not fear; you are worth more than many sparrows.

familiar.text: But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.

modern.text: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows. Confessing Christ (Matthew 10:32–33)

original.text: ἀλλὰ καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν πᾶσαι ἠρίθμηνται· ⸀μὴ φοβεῖσθε· πολλῶν στρουθίων διαφέρετε.

verses.restored: I say to you, everyone who confesses me before humans, the Son of Humanity will also confess before the messengers of the Divine.

familiar.text: Also I say unto you, Whosoever shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of man also confess before the angels of God:

modern.text: I tell you, everyone who confesses Me before men, the Son of Man will also confess him before the angels of God.

original.text: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, πᾶς ὃς ἂν ⸀ὁμολογήσῃ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὁμολογήσει ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ·

verses.restored: But the one denying me before humans will be denied before the messengers of the Divine.

familiar.text: But he that denieth me before men shall be denied before the angels of God.

modern.text: But whoever denies Me before men will be denied before the angels of God.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀρνησάμενός με ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπαρνηθήσεται ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Humanity will be released; but the one blaspheming against the holy Spirit will not be released.

familiar.text: And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost it shall not be forgiven.

modern.text: And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

original.text: καὶ πᾶς ὃς ἐρεῖ λόγον εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ τῷ δὲ εἰς τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα βλασφημήσαντι οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται.

verses.restored: When they bring you before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry how or what you should defend yourself with, or what you should say.

familiar.text: And when they bring you unto the synagogues, and unto magistrates, and powers, take ye no thought how or what thing ye shall answer, or what ye shall say:

modern.text: When you are brought before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.

original.text: ὅταν δὲ ⸀εἰσφέρωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐπὶ τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας, μὴ ⸀μεριμνήσητε πῶς ⸂ἢ τί⸃ ἀπολογήσησθε ἢ τί εἴπητε·

verses.restored: For the holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what it is necessary to say.

familiar.text: For the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.

modern.text: For at that time the Holy Spirit will teach you what you should say.” The Parable of the Rich Fool

original.text: τὸ γὰρ ἅγιον πνεῦμα διδάξει ὑμᾶς ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἃ δεῖ εἰπεῖν.

verses.restored: Someone from the crowd said to him, Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.

familiar.text: And one of the company said unto him, Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me.

modern.text: Someone in the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”

original.text: Εἶπεν δέ τις ⸂ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου αὐτῷ⸃· Διδάσκαλε, εἰπὲ τῷ ἀδελφῷ μου μερίσασθαι μετʼ ἐμοῦ τὴν κληρονομίαν.

verses.restored: He said to him, Human one, who appointed me judge or divider over you?

familiar.text: And he said unto him, Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?

modern.text: But Jesus replied, “Man, who appointed Me judge or executor between you?”

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἄνθρωπε, τίς με κατέστησεν ⸀κριτὴν ἢ μεριστὴν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς;

verses.restored: He said to them, Watch and guard yourselves from all greed, because one's life is not in the abundance of possessions.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.

modern.text: And He said to them, “Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὁρᾶτε καὶ φυλάσσεσθε ἀπὸ ⸀πάσης πλεονεξίας, ὅτι οὐκ ἐν τῷ περισσεύειν τινὶ ἡ ζωὴ ⸀αὐτοῦ ἐστιν ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων ⸀αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: He spoke a parable to them, saying, The land of a certain rich person produced abundantly.

familiar.text: And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully:

modern.text: Then He told them a parable: “The ground of a certain rich man produced an abundance.

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων· Ἀνθρώπου τινὸς πλουσίου εὐφόρησεν ἡ χώρα.

verses.restored: He reasoned within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have nowhere to gather my fruits?

familiar.text: And he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits?

modern.text: So he thought to himself, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to store my crops?’

original.text: καὶ διελογίζετο ἐν ⸀ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Τί ποιήσω, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχω ποῦ συνάξω τοὺς καρπούς μου;

verses.restored: He said, I will do this: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will gather all my grain and good things.

familiar.text: And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods.

modern.text: Then he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and will build bigger ones, and there I will store up all my grain and my goods.

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν· Τοῦτο ποιήσω· καθελῶ μου τὰς ἀποθήκας καὶ μείζονας οἰκοδομήσω, καὶ συνάξω ἐκεῖ πάντα ⸂τὸν σῖτον⸃ καὶ τὰ ἀγαθά μου,

verses.restored: I will say to my soul/life, Soul/life, you have many good things laid up for many years; rest, eat, drink, rejoice.

familiar.text: And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.

modern.text: Then I will say to myself, “You have plenty of good things laid up for many years. Take it easy. Eat, drink, and be merry!”’

original.text: καὶ ἐρῶ τῇ ψυχῇ μου· Ψυχή, ἔχεις πολλὰ ἀγαθὰ κείμενα εἰς ἔτη πολλά· ἀναπαύου, φάγε, πίε, εὐφραίνου.

verses.restored: But the Divine said to him, Foolish one, this night your soul/life is required from you; and what you prepared, whose will it be?

familiar.text: But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?

modern.text: But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life will be required of you. Then who will own what you have accumulated?’

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ θεός· ⸀Ἄφρων, ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ τὴν ψυχήν σου ⸀ἀπαιτοῦσιν ἀπὸ σοῦ· ἃ δὲ ἡτοίμασας, τίνι ἔσται;

verses.restored: So is the one treasuring for oneself and not being rich toward the Divine.

familiar.text: So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.

modern.text: This is how it will be for anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.” Do Not Worry (Matthew 6:25–34)

original.text: οὕτως ὁ θησαυρίζων ⸀ἑαυτῷ καὶ μὴ εἰς θεὸν πλουτῶν.

verses.restored: He said to his disciples, Because of this I say to you: do not worry about the life/soul, what you should eat, nor about the body, what you should wear.

familiar.text: And he said unto his disciples, Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat; neither for the body, what ye shall put on.

modern.text: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.

original.text: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Διὰ τοῦτο ⸂λέγω ὑμῖν⸃, μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ⸀ψυχῇ τί φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ ⸀σώματι τί ἐνδύσησθε.

verses.restored: For the life/soul is more than food, and the body more than clothing.

familiar.text: The life is more than meat, and the body is more than raiment.

modern.text: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.

original.text: ἡ ⸀γὰρ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος.

verses.restored: Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap; they have neither storeroom nor barn, and the Divine feeds them. How much more valuable are you than the birds?

familiar.text: Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap; which neither have storehouse nor barn; and God feedeth them: how much more are ye better than the fowls?

modern.text: Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn; yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!

original.text: κατανοήσατε τοὺς κόρακας ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν, οἷς οὐκ ἔστιν ταμεῖον οὐδὲ ἀποθήκη, καὶ ὁ θεὸς τρέφει αὐτούς· πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμεῖς διαφέρετε τῶν πετεινῶν.

verses.restored: Which of you by worrying is able to add a cubit to one's span of life?

familiar.text: And which of you with taking thought can add to his stature one cubit?

modern.text: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?

original.text: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται ⸂ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ προσθεῖναι⸃ ⸀πῆχυν;

verses.restored: If then you are not able to do even the smallest thing, why worry about the rest?

familiar.text: If ye then be not able to do that thing which is least, why take ye thought for the rest?

modern.text: So if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest?

original.text: εἰ οὖν ⸀οὐδὲ ἐλάχιστον δύνασθε, τί περὶ τῶν λοιπῶν μεριμνᾶτε;

verses.restored: Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither labor nor spin. Yet I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.

familiar.text: Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

modern.text: Consider how the lilies grow: They do not labor or spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.

original.text: κατανοήσατε τὰ κρίνα πῶς αὐξάνει· οὐ κοπιᾷ οὐδὲ νήθει· λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.

verses.restored: If the Divine so clothes the grass in the field, existing today and tomorrow thrown into the oven, how much more you, ones of little trust?

familiar.text: If then God so clothe the grass, which is to day in the field, and to morrow is cast into the oven; how much more will he clothe you, O ye of little faith?

modern.text: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more will He clothe you, O you of little faith!

original.text: εἰ δὲ ⸂ἐν ἀγρῷ τὸν χόρτον ὄντα σήμερον⸃ καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ⸀ἀμφιέζει, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι.

verses.restored: Do not seek what you should eat and what you should drink, and do not be suspended in anxious unrest.

familiar.text: And seek not ye what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind.

modern.text: And do not be concerned about what you will eat or drink. Do not worry about it.

original.text: καὶ ὑμεῖς μὴ ζητεῖτε τί φάγητε ⸀καὶ τί πίητε, καὶ μὴ μετεωρίζεσθε,

verses.restored: For all the nations of the world seek these things, and your Father knows that you need them.

familiar.text: For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: and your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things.

modern.text: For the Gentiles of the world strive after all these things, and your Father knows that you need them.

original.text: ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη τοῦ κόσμου ⸀ἐπιζητοῦσιν, ὑμῶν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ οἶδεν ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων.

verses.restored: Instead, seek his reign, and these things will be added to you.

familiar.text: But rather seek ye the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you.

modern.text: But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you. Treasures in Heaven (Matthew 6:19–21)

original.text: πλὴν ζητεῖτε τὴν βασιλείαν ⸀αὐτοῦ, καὶ ⸀ταῦτα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: Do not fear, little flock, because your Father delights to give you the reign.

familiar.text: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.

modern.text: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.

original.text: Μὴ φοβοῦ, τὸ μικρὸν ποίμνιον, ὅτι εὐδόκησεν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν δοῦναι ὑμῖν τὴν βασιλείαν.

verses.restored: Sell your possessions and give mercy-giving. Make for yourselves purses that do not grow old, unfailing treasure in the heavens, where thief does not come near and moth does not destroy.

familiar.text: Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.

modern.text: Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Provide yourselves with purses that will not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.

original.text: πωλήσατε τὰ ὑπάρχοντα ὑμῶν καὶ δότε ἐλεημοσύνην· ποιήσατε ἑαυτοῖς βαλλάντια μὴ παλαιούμενα, θησαυρὸν ἀνέκλειπτον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ὅπου κλέπτης οὐκ ἐγγίζει οὐδὲ σὴς διαφθείρει·

verses.restored: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

familiar.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

modern.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also. Readiness at Any Hour (Matthew 24:36–51; Mark 13:32–37)

original.text: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρὸς ὑμῶν, ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ καρδία ὑμῶν ἔσται.

verses.restored: Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning.

familiar.text: Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning;

modern.text: Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning.

original.text: Ἔστωσαν ὑμῶν αἱ ὀσφύες περιεζωσμέναι καὶ οἱ λύχνοι καιόμενοι,

verses.restored: Be like people waiting for their lord when he returns from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him immediately.

familiar.text: And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding; that when he cometh and knocketh, they may open unto him immediately.

modern.text: Then you will be like servants waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him at once.

original.text: καὶ ὑμεῖς ὅμοιοι ἀνθρώποις προσδεχομένοις τὸν κύριον ἑαυτῶν πότε ἀναλύσῃ ἐκ τῶν γάμων, ἵνα ἐλθόντος καὶ κρούσαντος εὐθέως ἀνοίξωσιν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: Blessed/flourishing are those servants whom the lord, coming, will find watching. Amen, I say to you: he will gird himself, make them recline, and come serve them.

familiar.text: Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say unto you, that he shall gird himself, and make them to sit down to meat, and will come forth and serve them.

modern.text: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds on watch when he returns. Truly I tell you, he will dress himself to serve and will have them recline at the table, and he himself will come and wait on them.

original.text: μακάριοι οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι, οὓς ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος εὑρήσει γρηγοροῦντας· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι περιζώσεται καὶ ἀνακλινεῖ αὐτοὺς καὶ παρελθὼν διακονήσει αὐτοῖς.

verses.restored: If he comes in the second watch or in the third and finds them so, blessed/flourishing are those ones.

familiar.text: And if he shall come in the second watch, or come in the third watch, and find them so, blessed are those servants.

modern.text: Even if he comes in the second or third watch of the night and finds them alert, those servants will be blessed.

original.text: ⸂κἂν ἐν τῇ δευτέρᾳ κἂν⸃ ἐν τῇ τρίτῃ φυλακῇ ἔλθῃ καὶ εὕρῃ οὕτως, μακάριοί ⸀εἰσιν ἐκεῖνοι.

verses.restored: Know this: if the house-master had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have allowed his house to be dug through.

familiar.text: And this know, that if the goodman of the house had known what hour the thief would come, he would have watched, and not have suffered his house to be broken through.

modern.text: But understand this: If the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.

original.text: Τοῦτο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ ὥρᾳ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται, ⸂οὐκ ἂν⸃ ἀφῆκεν ⸀διορυχθῆναι τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: You also must become ready, because the Son of Humanity comes at an hour you do not expect.

familiar.text: Be ye therefore ready also: for the Son of man cometh at an hour when ye think not.

modern.text: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.”

original.text: καὶ ⸀ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι, ὅτι ᾗ ὥρᾳ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται.

verses.restored: Peter said, Lord, are you saying this parable to us, or also to all?

familiar.text: Then Peter said unto him, Lord, speakest thou this parable unto us, or even to all?

modern.text: “Lord,” said Peter, “are You addressing this parable to us, or to everyone else as well?”

original.text: Εἶπεν ⸀δὲ ὁ Πέτρος· Κύριε, πρὸς ἡμᾶς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγεις ἢ καὶ πρὸς πάντας;

verses.restored: The Lord said, Who then is the trustworthy and wise steward whom the lord will appoint over his household servants to give the food allowance at the proper time?

familiar.text: And the Lord said, Who then is that faithful and wise steward, whom his lord shall make ruler over his household, to give them their portion of meat in due season?

modern.text: And the Lord answered, “Who then is the faithful and wise manager, whom the master puts in charge of his servants to give them their portion at the proper time?

original.text: ⸂καὶ εἶπεν⸃ ὁ κύριος· Τίς ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ πιστὸς οἰκονόμος, ⸀ὁ φρόνιμος, ὃν καταστήσει ὁ κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς θεραπείας αὐτοῦ τοῦ διδόναι ἐν καιρῷ ⸀τὸ σιτομέτριον;

verses.restored: Blessed/flourishing is that servant whom his lord, coming, will find doing so.

familiar.text: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.

modern.text: Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.

original.text: μακάριος ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος, ὃν ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει ποιοῦντα οὕτως·

verses.restored: Truly I say to you, he will appoint him over all his possessions.

familiar.text: Of a truth I say unto you, that he will make him ruler over all that he hath.

modern.text: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.

original.text: ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοῦ καταστήσει αὐτόν.

verses.restored: But if that servant says in his heart, My lord delays coming, and begins to beat the male and female servants, to eat and drink and become drunk,

familiar.text: But and if that servant say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; and shall begin to beat the menservants and maidens, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken;

modern.text: But suppose that servant says in his heart, ‘My master will be a long time in coming,’ and he begins to beat the menservants and maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk.

original.text: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃ ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἔρχεσθαι, καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς παῖδας καὶ τὰς παιδίσκας, ἐσθίειν τε καὶ πίνειν καὶ μεθύσκεσθαι,

verses.restored: the lord of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him apart and place his portion with the untrustworthy.

familiar.text: The lord of that servant will come in a day when he looketh not for him, and at an hour when he is not aware, and will cut him in sunder, and will appoint him his portion with the unbelievers.

modern.text: The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate. Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the unbelievers.

original.text: ἥξει ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ οὐ προσδοκᾷ καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ᾗ οὐ γινώσκει, καὶ διχοτομήσει αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀπίστων θήσει.

verses.restored: That servant who knew the will of his lord and did not prepare or act according to his will will be beaten with many blows.

familiar.text: And that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.

modern.text: That servant who knows his master’s will but does not get ready or follow his instructions will be beaten with many blows.

original.text: ἐκεῖνος δὲ ὁ δοῦλος ὁ γνοὺς τὸ θέλημα τοῦ κυρίου ⸀αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ ἑτοιμάσας ⸀ἢ ποιήσας πρὸς τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ δαρήσεται πολλάς·

verses.restored: But the one not knowing, yet doing things worthy of blows, will be beaten with few. From everyone to whom much was given, much will be required; and from the one to whom much was entrusted, they will ask more.

familiar.text: But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.

modern.text: But the one who unknowingly does things worthy of punishment will be beaten with few blows. From everyone who has been given much, much will be required; and from him who has been entrusted with much, even more will be demanded. Not Peace but Division (Micah 7:1–6; Matthew 10:34–39)

original.text: ὁ δὲ μὴ γνοὺς ποιήσας δὲ ἄξια πληγῶν δαρήσεται ὀλίγας. παντὶ δὲ ᾧ ἐδόθη πολύ, πολὺ ζητηθήσεται παρʼ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ᾧ παρέθεντο πολύ, περισσότερον αἰτήσουσιν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: I came to cast fire upon the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled.

familiar.text: I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I, if it be already kindled?

modern.text: I have come to ignite a fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!

original.text: Πῦρ ἦλθον βαλεῖν ⸀ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ τί θέλω εἰ ἤδη ἀνήφθη;

verses.restored: I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is completed.

familiar.text: But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished!

modern.text: But I have a baptism to undergo, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!

original.text: βάπτισμα δὲ ἔχω βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ πῶς συνέχομαι ἕως ⸀ὅτου τελεσθῇ.

verses.restored: Do you think I came to give peace on the earth? No, I say to you, but rather division.

familiar.text: Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:

modern.text: Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth? No, I tell you, but division.

original.text: δοκεῖτε ὅτι εἰρήνην παρεγενόμην δοῦναι ἐν τῇ γῇ; οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλʼ ἢ διαμερισμόν.

verses.restored: For from now on five in one house will be divided: three against two and two against three.

familiar.text: For from henceforth there shall be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.

modern.text: From now on, five in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three.

original.text: ἔσονται γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν πέντε ἐν ⸂ἑνὶ οἴκῳ⸃ διαμεμερισμένοι, τρεῖς ἐπὶ δυσὶν καὶ δύο ἐπὶ τρισίν,

verses.restored: They will be divided father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.

familiar.text: The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.

modern.text: They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law. ” Interpreting the Present Time (Matthew 16:1–4; Mark 8:11–13)

original.text: ⸀διαμερισθήσονται πατὴρ ἐπὶ υἱῷ καὶ υἱὸς ἐπὶ πατρί, μήτηρ ⸀ἐπὶ ⸀θυγατέρα καὶ θυγάτηρ ἐπὶ ⸂τὴν μητέρα⸃, πενθερὰ ἐπὶ τὴν νύμφην αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφη ἐπὶ τὴν ⸀πενθεράν.

verses.restored: He also said to the crowds, When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately you say, A shower is coming, and so it happens.

familiar.text: And he said also to the people, When ye see a cloud rise out of the west, straightway ye say, There cometh a shower; and so it is.

modern.text: Then Jesus said to the crowds, “As soon as you see a cloud rising in the west, you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and that is what happens.

original.text: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις· Ὅταν ⸀ἴδητε νεφέλην ἀνατέλλουσαν ⸀ἐπὶ δυσμῶν, εὐθέως λέγετε ⸀ὅτι Ὄμβρος ἔρχεται, καὶ γίνεται οὕτως·

verses.restored: When you see a south wind blowing, you say, There will be scorching heat, and it happens.

familiar.text: And when ye see the south wind blow, ye say, There will be heat; and it cometh to pass.

modern.text: And when the south wind blows, you say, ‘It will be hot,’ and it is.

original.text: καὶ ὅταν νότον πνέοντα, λέγετε ὅτι Καύσων ἔσται, καὶ γίνεται.

verses.restored: Hypocrites, you know how to discern the face of earth and heaven, but how do you not know how to discern this time?

familiar.text: Ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky and of the earth; but how is it that ye do not discern this time?

modern.text: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and sky. Why don’t you know how to interpret the present time? Reconciling with an Adversary (Matthew 5:21–26)

original.text: ὑποκριταί, τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γῆς καὶ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν, τὸν ⸂δὲ καιρὸν⸃ τοῦτον πῶς ⸂οὐκ οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν⸃;

verses.restored: Why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

familiar.text: Yea, and why even of yourselves judge ye not what is right?

modern.text: And why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?

original.text: Τί δὲ καὶ ἀφʼ ἑαυτῶν οὐ κρίνετε τὸ δίκαιον;

verses.restored: As you go with your opponent before a ruler, on the way give effort to be released from him, lest he drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.

familiar.text: When thou goest with thine adversary to the magistrate, as thou art in the way, give diligence that thou mayest be delivered from him; lest he hale thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and the officer cast thee into prison.

modern.text: Make every effort to reconcile with your adversary while you are on your way to the magistrate. Otherwise, he may drag you off to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and the officer may throw you into prison.

original.text: ὡς γὰρ ὑπάγεις μετὰ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου σου ἐπʼ ἄρχοντα, ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ δὸς ἐργασίαν ἀπηλλάχθαι ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ, μήποτε κατασύρῃ σε πρὸς τὸν κριτήν, καὶ ὁ κριτής σε ⸀παραδώσει τῷ πράκτορι, καὶ ὁ πράκτωρ σε ⸀βαλεῖ εἰς φυλακήν.

verses.restored: I say to you, you will certainly not come out from there until you have paid the last small coin.

familiar.text: I tell thee, thou shalt not depart thence, till thou hast paid the very last mite.

modern.text: I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny. ”

original.text: λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως ⸂καὶ τὸ⸃ ἔσχατον λεπτὸν ἀποδῷς.
